rebuild: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/loadout/build_loadout_assets.py -- [--renders DIR] [--only kind,...]; then Godot --headless --import (hard time limit)

licence.models: Original procedural models generated by this project's script; no third-party geometry except the arrow mesh reused from assets/weapons/arrow.glb (also generated by this project, tools/models/arrow.py).
licence.textures: Derived from CC0 1.0 Poly Haven maps already in assets/polyhaven (public domain dedication, no attribution required; see assets/polyhaven/MANIFEST.json for each source URL), recoloured and downsampled; horn, brass and sinew maps are procedural. Nothing was downloaded.
licence.provenance: These models are not derived from the extracted Actor_B game data. Their placement frames follow data/loadout/carry_gear.json, which was measured on the Actor_B rig.

conventions.axes: Godot / glTF (+Y up). Items fitted to a weapon use that weapon's model frame (WeaponModels / ThrowableModels) and are added as a child of the weapon model with an identity transform; body items have their own frame with the origin at the attach point.
conventions.markers: glTF empties at the root (identity rotation unless 'xform' is given); they import as Node3D and LoadoutModels.build() turns them into Marker3D children of the model root
conventions.materials: PBR: base colour, normal (OpenGL +Y), metallic-roughness (G roughness, B metal); tileable maps with UVs in metres / tile size; images embedded as JPEG

assets.title: Leather back quiver with arrows
assets.pivot: centre of the mouth (the stow origin of quiver.quiver)
assets.axes: +Y out of the mouth along the quiver, +Z away from the wearer's back, +X = Y x Z (the side seam and its fringe are on -X, toward the spine when worn behind the right shoulder)

nodes.Quiver: leather tube, buckskin collar and fringe, rawhide bottom cup, side-seam welt and fringe, two strap tabs
nodes.Arrows: parent of Arrow_01..Arrow_24, linked duplicates of one mesh (QuiverArrow: the top 0.25 m of assets/weapons/arrow.glb, 302 tris); index order = fill order (centre first), show the first `count`

Mouth.role: origin: centre of the mouth; +Y out of the mouth, +Z away from the wearer's back

assets.history: Eastern Woodlands quivers of skin or bark were worn on the back (general practice, grade B in body_fit_history.md). Construction here (leather tube, buckskin collar, fringed side seam, rawhide cup) is a plausible reconstruction, not a copy of a specific surviving piece.

assets.axes: +Z along the chord from the plug to the spout, +Y up when hanging, +X = Y x Z; the curve bulges toward -X (away from the body in the reference placement) and 1.2 cm up

StrapBase.role: strap anchor at the plug end (top of the thong loop)

SpoutRing.role: carved spout ring groove where the strap is tied

StrapSpout.role: strap anchor at the spout end (top of the thong loop)

LoadoutHorn: procedural (cow horn: cream to amber, dark tip, growth rings)

assets.history: A bullock's horn on a strap over the left shoulder (Knox 1757, via the costume bible [M2]; grade A for the horn and strap, grade C for its place behind the right hip, loadout_design.md 2.6). Sized to the measured placement envelope (plug radius 3.2 cm, spout 1.8 cm, chord 0.195 m), so it reads as a horn, not a lump.

reference_bind_placement.note: model origin on the capsule's plug point, chord along plug -> spout, the curve's bulge toward the measured bend; local = spinec global rest affine_inverse() * bind

assets.title: Pistol belt hook (and tuck point)
assets.frame: WeaponModels pistol frame (assets/weapons/pistol.glb): add as a child of the pistol model with an identity transform
assets.axes: pistol axes: -Z muzzle, +Y top, +X lock side; the hook is on the left flat (-X)

nodes.BeltHook: flat bright steel hook, 12.6 cm x 9.5 mm, fixed by the rear side nail on the brass side plate and running forward along the fore-stock 7.6 mm off it (room for a 5 mm belt), spoon-shaped free end

Hook.role: belt seat: centre of a 4 cm belt pushed up to the closed end of the hook (the belt runs along Y here, its width along Z, its thickness along X)

HookScrew.role: rear side nail through the hook

Tuck.role: where a belt or sash crosses the pistol when it is thrust through (just ahead of the lock and guard)

carry_points: L_hip.pistol / back_right.pistol: tucked (hook hidden or unused; use the Tuck marker)
assets.history: A long steel belt hook on the left side of the stock, fixed by the rear lock screw, let a pistol be carried in a waist or cross belt; the 1756 pattern long sea-service pistol had one (loadout_design.md [W2][W3], grade B). Hooked with its left flat to the belt the pistol hangs lock out.

assets.title: Pistol sling holster loop (one per chest pistol)
assets.frame: WeaponModels pistol frame (assets/weapons/pistol.glb): add as a child of each stowed chest pistol with an identity transform
assets.axes: pistol axes (-Z muzzle, +Y top, +X lock side); the loop wraps the -X side and is sewn to a band lying on the +X (lock) side, as carry_gear.json chest_R / chest_L carry the pistol along the band, lock toward the body. Mirror x for a lock-out variant.

nodes.PistolLoop: 2.6 cm leather loop round the fore-stock just ahead of the lock (the lock and guard stop the pistol sliding through), sewn tabs and a patch on the band

LoopCentre.role: centre of the loop round the pistol's fore-stock

BandSeat.role: sling band centreline under the loop, on the outer face of the patch: ribbon anchor (the band runs along the pistol's Z here, its width along Y)

assets.history: One pistol hung from a thin shoulder belt (Highland soldiers of the 42nd, [W1], grade B); several pistols in holsters on one sling (Johnson 1724 on Blackbeard, [W4], grade C). Loops rather than bare hooks because the chest pistols in carry_gear.json face the band with the lock side.

band.route: right shoulder -> chest_R loop -> chest_L loop -> left hip -> back (buckle) -> right shoulder (runtime ribbon; bind-space route in strap_routes_bind.json)

integration_hooks: Load through scripts/loadout/loadout_models.gd: LoadoutModels.build(kind) instances assets/loadout/<kind>.glb, turns the marker empties into Marker3D children of the root and (quiver) converts Arrow_01..24 into one MultiMeshInstance3D; set_arrow_count(model, n), slot_transforms(model, prefix), set_display(model, on), quiver_nocks_offset(model), manifest_entry(kind). Tested by tests/loadout/test_loadout_models.gd.

Weapon-frame items (musket_sling, pistol_belt_hook, pistol_sling_loop, tomahawk_frog, bow_cord) are children of the STOWED weapon copy with an identity transform. spear_pair_tie and dart_bundle are placed at the long_A / long_B stow and the stowed spears / darts are its children at the Spear_n / Dart_n markers (ThrowableModels spear / atlatl_dart). Hide BowCord on the bow in hand; keep the musket sling ends on the musket in hand and show SlingTaut there.

Straps: assets/loadout/strap_routes_bind.json (tools/loadout/render_loadout_on_body.py) gives every StrapRibbon its anchors in order: item markers (StrapFront/StrapRear, StrapTop/StrapBottom, ThongUpper/ThongLower, StrapBase/StrapSpout, BandSeat) and bind-space body anchors (shoulder tops, chest, sternum, ribs, under the arms, hips, back), the inner-to-outer layer order, width and the bind-pose length (musket sling 1.59 m, quiver strap 1.06 m, horn strap 0.99 m, pistol sling 1.37 m closed).

Quiver height (recommend changing carry_gear.json): with the stow as stated (origin = the quiver's Mouth at y 1.567 m) the fletching spans 1.57-1.71 m and the nocks reach 1.73 m, above the hat, while the source arrow reach (actor_b-p-bow-reload--part) moves the hand from 1.20 m to 1.47 m by 0.4 s (handoff_survey.md). Placed with stow * LoadoutModels.quiver_nocks_offset(model) (the nocks at the stow origin, as the body-fit candidate generator read the capsule) the fletching spans 1.40-1.54 m, in the hand's path. Screens: onbody_musket_bow.png vs onbody_musket_bow_quiver_at_nocks.png. Re-run the survey for the lowered quiver before adopting it.

Right-hip pistol hook: carry_gear.json R_hip.pistol puts the pistol's grip on the belt; the hook's belt seat (Hook marker, 8.7 cm from the grip in the pistol frame) lands at bind (-0.181, 0.929, 0.105), 5.2 cm off the baked belt. For the hook to seat, move the pistol by -Hook in its own frame (stow * Transform3D(Basis(), -Hook)) and re-run the survey for that placement, or accept the gap (it is on the body side, hidden by the pistol from the gameplay camera).

Chest pistols: the chest_R and chest_L loops' band seats are at bind (0.014, 1.066, 0.148) and (0.125, 1.133, 0.146): 13 cm apart with the left one 6.7 cm HIGHER, and the two pistols lie parallel 12.6 cm apart across the band direction, so one baldric from the right shoulder to the left hip zig-zags through them (onbody_two_braces*.png). Suggested fix for the loadout design: keep chest_R on the band and move the second sling pistol down the same band toward the left side under the arm (the Highland carry [W1]), then re-measure. PistolLoop is sewn on the pistol's +X (lock) side because both placements put the lock toward the body; mirror it in x for lock-out placements.

back_2.tomahawk: the stacked second tomahawk (4.5 cm out, 4 cm up) leaves its frog's belt seat 6.5 cm off the belt; hang its frog on the belt beside the first (a shift along the belt) or from the first frog. back.tomahawk's frog seat is 1.2 cm from the belt.

L_hip.pistol (thrust through the belt, lock in): its Tuck point (where a belt crosses a thrust-through pistol, just ahead of the lock) is 15 cm below the belt at bind (0.212, 0.786, 0.080); a tucked pistol rests on the belt by its lock and guard, so that placement should rise about 12-15 cm (or become a hooked carry, lock out, with the belt hook). BeltHook is not shown on tucked pistols.

Musket sling: the swivel opening of musket.glb is 2.5 cm, so the strap is 2.3 cm wide at the ends; use 2.3 cm for the musket sling ribbon (loadout_design.md 4 says 3.5 cm). In long_A the rear swivel sits at mid-back (StrapRear at y 1.32 m, because the stowed musket's wrist is at y 1.115 m), so the route closes from the right lower ribs under the right arm to the rear swivel, not via the right hip.

Powder horn: reference_bind_placement is the model -> bind transform on spinec along the measured horn capsules; the customizer's horn_node() change (loadout_design.md 2.6) can bake this mesh there, or the loadout can place it rigidly with the 30 deg yield. The legacy body's baked horn strap still runs to the old right-hip place; the horn_strap route in strap_routes_bind.json goes plug staple -> left shoulder -> chest -> under the right arm -> spout ring.

Hidden display parts (powder_horn StrapPreview, spear_pair_tie / dart_bundle ThongPreview, musket_sling SlingTaut) are for world pickups, racks and the camp chest; on the body the straps are StrapRibbon ribbons through the markers.
